question:
A 44-year-old female patient with multiple bilateral lower extremity and pelvic fractures from a motor
vehicle accident develops pulseless electrical activity 16 hours after hospital admission. During the
subsequent code, despite CPR efforts, the patient expires. Post-mortem examination reveals massive
pulmonary embolism and hemorrhage in the pons, thalami, and putamen. Investigation shows that
during resuscitation, a code team member erroneously administered intravenous boluses using 1:1000
epinephrine (intended for intramuscular use in anaphylaxis) instead of the correct 1:10,000 preparation
(intended for intravenous use in cardiac arrest). Which of the following hospital interventions would be
most effective in preventing similar medication errors? Answer Choices: (A) Installing electronic
medication verification systems in crash carts (B) Using color-coded syringes for different epinephrine
concentrations (C) Requiring documentation of medication concentration verification (D) Implementing
mandatory double-checking of medication concentrations during codes (E) Storing epinephrine
preparations for intramuscular injection in autoinjectors (F) Creating separate crash carts for cardiac
arrest and anaphylaxis (G) Implementing barcode scanning for emergency medications (H) Requiring
pharmacy preparation of all epinephrine doses (I) Labeling prefilled epinephrine syringes with the
correct indication instead of concentration (J) Standardizing all epinephrine concentrations to a single
formulation
 A. Storing epinephrine preparations for intramuscular injection in autoinjectors
B. Using color-coded syringes for different epinephrine concentrations
C. Standardizing all epinephrine concentrations to a single formulation
D. Implementing mandatory double-checking of medication concentrations during codes
E. Requiring pharmacy preparation of all epinephrine doses
F. Implementing barcode scanning for emergency medications
G. Installing electronic medication verification systems in crash carts
H. Labeling prefilled epinephrine syringes with the correct indication instead of concentration
I. Requiring documentation of medication concentration verification
J. Creating separate crash carts for cardiac arrest and anaphylaxis
